svg.title: SA-CCR EAD calculation reference
svg.desc: Formulas and supervisory parameters of the standardised approach for counterparty credit risk under Basel CRE52 and the EU CRR, as implemented in VBA-SACCR-Toolkit.

svg.text: Basis and volatility transactions form their own hedging sets per label, with SF × 0.5 (basis) or SF × 5 (volatility) (CRE52.46–52.47; CRR Art. 280).

svg.text: CRR vs Basel — where the toolkit's results can differ

text.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: • IR bucket 1: E ≤ 1 y under CRR, E < 1 y under Basel (exactly 1 y: bucket 1 vs bucket 2).

text.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: • Other risks (OT, SF 8%) exist only under CRR; Basel maps them to the primary risk driver's class.

text.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: • CRR shifts IR and commodity option deltas by the regulatory λ; Basel uses the λ entered.

text.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: • IR sum of absolute bucket values: Basel option only. Climatic conditions: own CO hedging set under CRR.

text.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Sources: BCBS CRE52 (in force 2023-01-01); Regulation (EU) No 575/2013, consolidated 26.06.2026; Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/931 as amended by 2025/855.

text.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Conventions: 365 days per year for S, E, M, T; 250 business days per year for floors and MPOR. SA-CCR gives the EAD; risk weights come from the credit-risk framework.
